# Controlling Windows: sound, screen, theme, power, timers, clipboard, opening and closing apps.
# Sensei helpers used here live in core/SenseiTools.psm1 and were tested on this PC.

## Sound

? set the volume to {percent} | volume {percent} | change volume to {percent} | put the sound at {percent} | turn the volume to {percent} | turn the volume down to {percent} | turn the sound down to {percent} | turn the volume up to {percent} | turn it up to {percent}
Set-AudioVolume -Percent {{percent}}
= Sets the speaker volume to {percent}% (Sensei helper).

? mute | mute the volume | mute the sound | mute my pc | silence the computer | turn the sound off
Set-AudioVolume -Mute
= Mutes the speakers.

? unmute | unmute the volume | unmute the sound | turn the sound on | sound on
Set-AudioVolume -Unmute
= Unmutes the speakers.

? volume up | turn the volume up | louder | increase volume by {percent} | make it louder | volume up {percent}
Set-AudioVolume -Up {{percent}}
= Raises the volume by {percent} points.
& percent=10

? volume down | turn the volume down | quieter | decrease volume by {percent} | make it quieter | lower the volume
Set-AudioVolume -Down {{percent}}
= Lowers the volume by {percent} points.
& percent=10

? max volume | full volume | volume to maximum | loudest
Set-AudioVolume -Percent 100
= Sets the volume to 100%.

? what is the volume | current volume | how loud is it | volume level | is the sound muted
Get-AudioVolume
= Shows the volume in percent and whether it is muted.

? say {text} | speak {text} | read {text} aloud | text to speech {text}
Out-Speech -Text '{{text}}'
= Reads "{text}" aloud with the Windows voice.

? read {file} aloud | speak the text of {file}
Out-Speech -Text (Get-Content -Path "{{folder}}\{{file}}" -Raw)
= Reads the contents of {file} aloud.
& folder=.

? sound settings | open sound settings | change speakers | output device
Start-Process "ms-settings:sound"
= Opens Sound settings, where you pick speakers and microphone.

? sound devices | audio devices | speakers and microphones | list sound cards
Get-CimInstance Win32_SoundDevice | Select-Object Name, Status
= Lists the sound devices.

## Screen

? set brightness to {percent} | set screen brightness to {percent} | brightness {percent} | screen brightness {percent} | change the brightness to {percent} | dim the screen to {percent}
Set-ScreenBrightness -Percent {{percent}}
= Sets the laptop screen brightness to {percent}% (Sensei helper).

? brightness up | increase brightness | make the screen brighter
Set-ScreenBrightness -Percent ([math]::Min(100, (Get-ScreenBrightness).BrightnessPercent + 20))
= Makes the screen 20 points brighter.

? brightness down | decrease brightness | make the screen darker | dim the screen
Set-ScreenBrightness -Percent ([math]::Max(0, (Get-ScreenBrightness).BrightnessPercent - 20))
= Makes the screen 20 points darker.

? what is the brightness | current brightness | how bright is the screen
Get-ScreenBrightness
= Shows the screen brightness in percent.

? dark mode | turn on dark mode | switch to dark theme | dark theme | night mode for windows
Set-DarkMode
= Switches Windows and apps to dark mode.

? is dark mode on | which theme is on | am I in dark mode
if ((Get-ItemProperty 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize').AppsUseLightTheme -eq 0) { 'Dark mode is on.' } else { 'Light mode is on.' }
= Tells you whether Windows uses dark or light mode.

? light mode | turn off dark mode | switch to light theme | light theme
Set-DarkMode -Off
= Switches Windows and apps to light mode.

? set wallpaper to {file} | change my wallpaper to {file} | use {file} as wallpaper | make {file} my background | change the desktop background to {file}
Set-Wallpaper -Path "{{folder}}\{{file}}"
= Sets {file} as the desktop wallpaper.
& folder=.

? night light | turn on night light | blue light filter
Start-Process "ms-settings:nightlight"
= Opens Night light settings (Windows has no command to switch it directly).

? screen resolution | what resolution is my screen | refresh rate | display info
Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select-Object Name, CurrentHorizontalResolution, CurrentVerticalResolution, CurrentRefreshRate
= Shows the resolution and refresh rate of each display adapter.

? monitors | connected displays | which monitors are connected
Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/wmi -ClassName WmiMonitorID -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{ Maker = -join [char[]]($_.ManufacturerName -ne 0); Model = -join [char[]]($_.UserFriendlyName -ne 0); Serial = -join [char[]]($_.SerialNumberID -ne 0) } }
= Lists the connected monitors with maker and model.

? display settings | change resolution | scale settings | open display settings
Start-Process "ms-settings:display"
= Opens Display settings.

? take a screenshot | screenshot | capture the screen | print screen | save a screenshot
Save-Screenshot
= Saves the whole screen as a PNG in Pictures\Screenshots (Sensei helper).

? take a screenshot in {seconds} | screenshot after {seconds} | delayed screenshot
Save-Screenshot -Delay {{seconds}}
= Waits {seconds} seconds, then saves the whole screen in Pictures\Screenshots.
& seconds=5

? screenshot of an area | snip | snipping tool | screenshot of part of the screen | screen clip
Start-Process "ms-screenclip:"
= Opens the snipping overlay so you can drag over the area to capture.

? open the screenshots folder | where are my screenshots | show me my screenshots folder
Invoke-Item "$([Environment]::GetFolderPath('MyPictures'))\Screenshots"
= Opens Pictures\Screenshots.

? show hidden files in explorer | show file extensions | show hidden files and extensions in file explorer
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced' -Name Hidden -Value 1; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced' -Name HideFileExt -Value 0; 'Explorer now shows hidden files and file extensions (reopen its windows).'
= Makes File Explorer show hidden files and file extensions.

? hide hidden files in explorer | hide file extensions again
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced' -Name Hidden -Value 2; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Advanced' -Name HideFileExt -Value 1; 'Explorer hides hidden files and extensions again.'
= Puts File Explorer back to hiding hidden files and extensions.

? minimize all windows | show the desktop | hide all windows
(New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application).MinimizeAll()
= Minimizes every window.

? restore windows | undo minimize all | bring windows back
(New-Object -ComObject Shell.Application).UndoMinimizeALL()
= Restores the windows minimized by "minimize all".

## Power

? lock the pc | lock my computer | lock screen | lock windows | lock
rundll32.exe user32.dll,LockWorkStation
= Locks Windows immediately.

? sleep | put the pc to sleep | sleep mode | go to sleep | suspend
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; [void][System.Windows.Forms.Application]::SetSuspendState('Suspend', $false, $false)
= Puts the PC to sleep now.

? sleep in {minutes} | put the pc to sleep in {minutes} | sleep timer {minutes} | go to sleep in {minutes}
Start-SleepTimer -Minutes {{minutes}}
= Puts the PC to sleep in {minutes} minutes. Cancel it with "cancel shutdown" (Sensei helper).

? turn off the screen | screen off | turn off the display | switch off the monitor | blank the screen
Set-ScreenOff
= Turns the display off now; move the mouse to wake it (Sensei helper).

? hibernate | hibernate the pc
shutdown.exe /h
= Hibernates the PC now (only works when hibernation is enabled).

? sign out | log off | log out | sign me out
shutdown.exe /l
= Signs you out of Windows now. Save your work first.

? shut down | shut down the pc | turn off the computer | power off | shut down now
Stop-Computer
= Shuts down the PC right away.

? restart | restart the pc | reboot now | restart the computer | restart windows
Restart-Computer
= Restarts the PC right away.

? shut down at {time} | turn off the pc at {time} | shutdown at {time} | power off at {time}
Start-Shutdown -At '{{time}}'
= Shuts down at {time}. Cancel it with "cancel shutdown".

? shut down in {minutes} | turn off the pc in {minutes} | shutdown timer {minutes} | power off after {minutes} | shut down after {minutes}
Start-Shutdown -InMinutes {{minutes}}
= Shuts down in {minutes} minutes. Cancel it with "cancel shutdown".

? restart in {minutes} | reboot in {minutes} | restart after {minutes}
Start-Shutdown -InMinutes {{minutes}} -Restart
= Restarts in {minutes} minutes. Cancel it with "cancel shutdown".

? restart at {time} | reboot at {time}
Start-Shutdown -At '{{time}}' -Restart
= Restarts at {time}. Cancel it with "cancel shutdown".

? cancel shutdown | abort shutdown | stop the shutdown timer | cancel restart | do not shut down
Stop-Shutdown
= Cancels a scheduled shutdown or restart.

? restart into bios | restart to uefi | open bios settings
shutdown.exe /r /fw /t 0
= Restarts straight into the BIOS/UEFI setup.
! admin

? restart to advanced startup | restart into recovery | boot to safe mode options
shutdown.exe /r /o /t 0
= Restarts into the advanced startup menu (safe mode, recovery, startup repair).

? never sleep | set the pc to never sleep | keep the pc awake | disable sleep | stop the pc from sleeping | turn off sleep
powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac 0; powercfg /change standby-timeout-dc 0; 'Sleep is off (plugged in and on battery).'
= Turns automatic sleep off.

? sleep after {minutes} of inactivity | set sleep timeout to {minutes} | sleep timeout {minutes} | automatic sleep after {minutes}
powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac {{minutes}}; powercfg /change standby-timeout-dc {{minutes}}; 'Sleep after {{minutes}} minutes.'
= Sleeps automatically after {minutes} minutes without use.

? screen off after {minutes} | turn the display off after {minutes} | screen timeout {minutes}
powercfg /change monitor-timeout-ac {{minutes}}; powercfg /change monitor-timeout-dc {{minutes}}; 'Screen turns off after {{minutes}} minutes.'
= Turns the screen off after {minutes} minutes without use.

? never turn off the screen | keep the screen on | disable screen timeout
powercfg /change monitor-timeout-ac 0; powercfg /change monitor-timeout-dc 0; 'The screen stays on.'
= Keeps the screen on.

? power plans | which power plan | list power plans
powercfg /list
= Lists power plans; the active one has a star.

? high performance mode | best performance | power plan high performance
powercfg /setactive SCHEME_MIN; powercfg /getactivescheme
= Switches to the High performance power plan (if your PC offers it).

? balanced power plan | balanced mode
powercfg /setactive SCHEME_BALANCED; powercfg /getactivescheme
= Switches to the Balanced power plan.

? power saver | battery saver mode | power saving plan
powercfg /setactive SCHEME_MAX; powercfg /getactivescheme
= Switches to the Power saver plan (if your PC offers it).

? power settings | sleep settings | open power options
Start-Process "ms-settings:powersleep"
= Opens Power & sleep settings.

## Timers and reminders

? timer {minutes} | set a timer for {minutes} | start a {minutes} timer | countdown {minutes} | alarm in {minutes} | {minutes} timer
Start-Timer -Seconds {{seconds}}
= Pops up and beeps in {minutes} minutes; runs in the background (Sensei helper).
& seconds=300 ; minutes=5

? remind me to {text} in {minutes} | reminder in {minutes} to {text} | remind me in {minutes} to {text}
Start-Timer -Seconds {{seconds}} -Message '{{text}}'
= Pops up "{text}" in {minutes} minutes.
& seconds=600 ; minutes=10

? remind me at {time} to {text} | reminder at {time}
$m = [math]::Ceiling(((Get-Date '{{time}}') - (Get-Date)).TotalMinutes); if ($m -le 0) { $m += 1440 }; Start-Timer -Minutes $m -Message '{{text}}'
= Pops up "{text}" at {time}.
& text=Reminder

? stopwatch | start a stopwatch | measure time
$global:SenseiWatch = [Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew(); 'Stopwatch started. Ask "stop the stopwatch" to see the time.'
= Starts a stopwatch in Sensei's session.

? stop the stopwatch | how long since the stopwatch | stopwatch time
if ($global:SenseiWatch) { $global:SenseiWatch.Stop(); 'Elapsed: {0:hh\:mm\:ss\.f}' -f $global:SenseiWatch.Elapsed } else { 'No stopwatch is running.' }
= Shows the time since the stopwatch started.

## Clipboard

? copy {text} to the clipboard | put {text} on the clipboard | clipboard {text}
Set-Clipboard -Value '{{text}}'; 'Copied.'
= Copies "{text}" to the clipboard.

? what is in the clipboard | show clipboard | paste | clipboard content
Get-Clipboard
= Prints the text on the clipboard.

? clear the clipboard | empty clipboard
Set-Clipboard -Value ' '; 'Clipboard cleared.'
= Replaces the clipboard content with a blank.

? copy {file} to the clipboard | copy the text of {file}
Get-Content -Path "{{folder}}\{{file}}" -Raw | Set-Clipboard; 'Copied the text of {{file}}.'
= Copies the text of {file} to the clipboard.
& folder=.

? clipboard history | open clipboard history
Start-Process "ms-settings:clipboard"
= Opens clipboard settings (press Win+V for the history).

## Apps

? open {app} | start {app} | launch {app} | run {app}
Start-Process "{{app|launch}}"
= Starts {app}.

? close {app} | quit {app} | exit {app} | close all {app} windows
Close-App -Name "{{app|process}}"
= Asks {app} to close normally (it may ask to save) (Sensei helper).

? kill {app} | force close {app} | end {app} | stop {app} | terminate {app} | {app} is frozen
Stop-Process -Name "{{app|process}}" -Force
= Ends every {app} process immediately (unsaved work is lost).

? restart {app} | relaunch {app} | reopen {app}
Close-App -Name "{{app|process}}" -Force; Start-Sleep -Seconds 1; Start-Process "{{app|launch}}"
= Closes {app} and starts it again.

? is {app} running | check if {app} is open | is {app} open
$p = Get-Process -Name "{{app|process}}" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($p) { "{{app|name}} is running ($(@($p).Count) processes)." } else { "{{app|name}} is not running." }
= Tells you whether {app} is running.

? how much memory does {app} use | ram used by {app} | {app} memory | how much ram is {app} using
$p = Get-Process -Name "{{app|process}}" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; if ($p) { "{{app|name}}: {0:N0} MB in {1} processes" -f (($p | Measure-Object WorkingSet64 -Sum).Sum / 1MB), @($p).Count } else { "{{app|name}} is not running." }
= Adds up the memory of all {app} processes.

? where is {app} installed | path of {app} | location of {app}
$p = Get-Process -Name "{{app|process}}" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Path | Select-Object -First 1; if ($p) { $p.Path } else { (Get-Command "{{app|launch}}" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source }
= Shows the program file of {app}.

? open settings | windows settings | settings app
Start-Process "ms-settings:"
= Opens Windows Settings.

? open {page} | {page} | go to {page} | show {page}
Start-Process "{{page}}"
= Opens that page of Windows Settings.

? open control panel | control panel
control.exe
= Opens the classic Control Panel.

? open task manager | task manager
Start-Process taskmgr
= Opens Task Manager.

? open device manager | device manager
Start-Process devmgmt.msc
= Opens Device Manager.

? open disk management | disk management | partitions tool
Start-Process diskmgmt.msc
= Opens Disk Management.

? open services | services window
Start-Process services.msc
= Opens the Services window.

? open event viewer | event viewer
Start-Process eventvwr.msc
= Opens Event Viewer.

? open registry editor | regedit
Start-Process regedit
= Opens the Registry Editor.

? open programs and features | uninstall programs window | add or remove programs
Start-Process appwiz.cpl
= Opens Programs and Features.

? open network connections | network adapters window | ncpa
Start-Process ncpa.cpl
= Opens Network Connections.

? open system properties | advanced system settings | environment variables window
Start-Process SystemPropertiesAdvanced.exe
= Opens System Properties (environment variables, performance, startup).

? open system information | msinfo | msinfo32
Start-Process msinfo32
= Opens the System Information tool.

? open resource monitor | resource monitor
Start-Process resmon
= Opens Resource Monitor (CPU, disk, network, memory per process).

? open a website {url} | open {url} | go to {url} | browse {url}
Start-Process "{{url}}"
= Opens {url} in your default browser.

? open {host} | go to {host} | open the website {host} | browse {host}
Start-Process "https://{{host}}"
= Opens https://{host} in your default browser.

? search the web for {text} | google {text} | search online for {text}
Start-Process "https://www.bing.com/search?q=$([uri]::EscapeDataString('{{text}}'))"
= Searches the web for "{text}" in your browser.

? open the recycle bin | show recycle bin
Start-Process "shell:RecycleBinFolder"
= Opens the Recycle Bin.

? empty the recycle bin | clear the recycle bin | empty trash
Clear-RecycleBin -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; 'Recycle Bin emptied.'
= Empties the Recycle Bin on all drives (this cannot be undone).

? restart explorer | taskbar is frozen | restart the start menu | restart the taskbar
Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force
= Restarts File Explorer and the taskbar; Windows starts it again automatically.

? open a new powershell window | new terminal | open terminal here
Start-Process pwsh -WorkingDirectory (Get-Location).Path
= Opens a new PowerShell window in the current folder.

? open powershell as administrator | admin terminal | run powershell as admin | elevated powershell
Start-Process pwsh -Verb RunAs
= Opens PowerShell as administrator (Windows asks first).

? open {file} as administrator | run {file} as admin
Start-Process -FilePath "{{folder}}\{{file}}" -Verb RunAs
= Runs {file} as administrator (Windows asks first).
& folder=.
